statement: One pipe fills a tank in 4 hours and another in 6 hours. An open drain empties it in 12 hours. With all three open, how long does filling take?

choices.misconception: I added the drain's rate instead of subtracting it, so all three pipes seemed to fill the tank.
I added the two filling rates and ignored the drain completely.
I averaged the two filling times, 4 and 6, and ignored the drain.
I added the two filling times, 4 + 6, and ignored the drain.

hints: Turn every pipe into a fraction of the tank per hour.
Write each pipe's contribution as tank per hour, make the drain negative, add all three, then take the reciprocal of the total to get the time.
One quarter plus one sixth minus one twelfth of the tank fills each hour.

solutions.reliable: Per hour the pipes add 1/4 and 1/6 and the drain removes 1/12, so the net rate is 3/12 + 2/12 - 1/12 = 1/3 of the tank per hour, and filling takes 3 hours. The transferable idea: rates add with signs while times do not, so a drain is simply a negative rate.
solutions.elegant: Working in twelfths of a tank makes the three numbers 3, 2 and minus 1, which total 4 twelfths.

whyOnTest: A drain in the problem makes signed rates essential, and ignoring it or subtracting times gives two of the choices.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
